correctness.rationale: Every derivation is D(A,v); when D is periodic, det A != 0 and its central row is uniquely conjugate to zero by tI-A=adj(A). Because char >=5, D^6=I means A is semisimple with sixth-root eigenvalues alpha,beta and trace alpha+beta also a sixth root. The reduced resultant has prime factors 2,3,7 only, so ratios are primitive cube roots except in characteristic seven, where every non-opposite sixth-root pair is permitted. Split, nonsplit and scalar centralizers give the displayed orbit sizes. Exact-order exclusions and the characteristic-seven order-three case are checked algebraically. Exhaustive prime-field matrix tests passed for p=5,7,11,13,19; these tests do not substitute for the all-field proof.

value.rationale: The earliest directly relevant work identifies order six as a distinguished minimal period for complex nonabelian Lie algebras, but does not give its finite-field orbit population. The new complete automorphism-orbit census for the smallest nonabelian Lie algebra separates rationally split and nonsplit periodic derivations, computes stabilizer-size strata and exhibits a quantified characteristic-seven jump. This motivated natural classification is useful as a quantitative base case for studying periodic derivations in larger nilpotent Lie algebras, independent of any conjectured downstream theorem.
